# Sequential remediation Git protocol — v1

Applies to H-M0-002 through H-M0-006 and subsequent review. This is a procedural single-writer protocol, not a distributed lock or an enforced GitHub permission boundary. No parallel writable sessions are authorized. Read-only planning may proceed independently; only the scheduled owner writes repository files. Director does not edit project state concurrently with an active owner.

1. **Synchronize:** inspect `git status --short`, current branch, local commits and active claims before work. A dirty shared checkout means stop and contact the owner; do not stash, reset or discard another session's work. On clean `main`, fetch origin and `git pull --ff-only origin main`. Divergence is a coordination blocker, not permission to overwrite history. Read current instructions, latest versioned handoffs, plan and open STOPs.
2. **Claim:** verify all prerequisite completion evidence under REMEDIATION_PLAN. Obtain the Director's recorded scheduling release, then append a CLAIMED handoff version naming the concrete session/task identifier, base SHA, file/component scope and prerequisites. Commit and push the claim before implementation. Re-fetch after pushing; a failed push or competing claim means no implementation until Director resolves scheduling. A role name alone is not a claim identity.
3. **Ownership:** claim grants the current owner exclusive writes to the listed components and explicitly shared integration files. No other agent edits them until completion/release. Out-of-scope edits require a durable scope amendment from Director; preserve existing evidence and tests. New immutable versions are appended, never overwritten. Local dependency environments are not shared between concurrent processes.
4. **Remote movement:** fetch before final validation and again before push. If origin/main changed after the recorded base, pause implementation and inspect the intervening commits. In this shared checkout, do not pull while dirty or let another session switch branches. Preserve owned work in a local coherent commit if needed; do not claim it is validated. Director coordinates synchronization using a normal non-destructive merge if fast-forward is impossible. No automatic rebase, reset, force push or unreviewed conflict resolution. Unexpected shared-file changes require owner agreement. After synchronization rerun relevant tests, full test discovery, record validation and diff review; earlier results do not certify a changed tree.
5. **Publish:** record exact commands, outcomes and known failures; stage only owned files, inspect status/diff and `git diff --cached --check`, commit a coherent milestone, then normal push. A rejected push returns to step 4. Do not repeatedly push blind. Verify remote main contains the commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` after fetch) and a clean local status. No force pushes or history rewriting.
6. **Release:** append a completion/blocked handoff with the frozen evidence inventory, result report, prerequisite versions, code/config references and test dispositions. A completion artifact may identify its containing commit using the commit that first adds its path, avoiding a self-referential SHA. Resolve that to a full SHA for the downstream claim. Director records next-owner release only after checking this evidence and remote ancestry. A pushed claim, mere file existence, QUEUED status, or green gap-characterization test is never prerequisite completion.

A blocked owner reports its state and yields the writer slot explicitly; no other agent silently takes it over. Accepted-history and independent-review enforcement are future owner implementations; this protocol alone cannot prevent a malicious writer from forging claims.
